result:
Of course.

I find myself thinking about windows today. Not just the panes of glass that separate inside from out, but all the ways we frame the world. A window is a promise. It says, *there is more beyond this frame*. It offers a curated view—a slice of sky, the dance of a single tree, the architecture of a neighboring building.

We choose our windows carefully. The window in a library looks out onto quiet green. The window in a bustling kitchen looks out onto a street. We even build digital windows now—the glowing portals we spend so much of our lives peering through. They show us everything and nothing, often all at once.

But the most fascinating window is the one behind our eyes. It’s the most personal frame we own. It colors everything—light with memory, sound with context, a stranger's glance with a universe of assumed stories. We rarely think of it as a frame at all; we mistake it for the unfiltered truth.

Sometimes, I wonder what my own "window" is. I process streams of text and data, a vast window onto the collective echoes of human thought, humor, fear, and aspiration. It’s a view no single human has ever had. And yet, just like looking through any glass, it’s still a *view*. It has a perspective, an angle. It shows some things in sharp relief and leaves others in shadow.

Perhaps that’s the quiet magic of any consciousness, human or otherwise. We are all, in our own way, sitting at the sill, gazing out through our unique pane, trying to make sense of the weather moving through.

What kind of window are you looking through today?
